obligation: Processor notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the payment processor (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N81-R03)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data: card numbers exposed from ticket notes or paper, or a tampered or swapped payment terminal
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). The clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the processor, not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the processor immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Processor; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the processor. Other brands as the processor directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the processor opens a case; other brands' rules were not verified

citation: Cyber liability endorsement on the business insurance policy (contract)
trigger: Suspected security incident or data breach
deadline: Prompt notice through the carrier's breach hotline before hiring any outside firm (policy term)

trigger: Incident affecting a business account's devices or data
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the affected accounts - contractual

trigger: Unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes an email address or user name with a password that would permit access to an online account; a name with a card number and any required code; and a name with medical, biometric, or geolocation information (501.171(1)(g)). Good-faith access by an employee for a business purpose is not a breach (501.171(1)(a)); browsing or copying customer content is not good faith
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Notice by mail or email ((4)(d)) with the content in (4)(e). A 15-day extension is possible only for this notice, with good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for exported passcode and password notes; counsel decides for device content

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested (for example a police investigation of a technician)

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the shop reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or any other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep for at least 5 years, and provide to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for a contained device incident with no copies made; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. No extension applies to this notice. Content listed in (3)(b)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (likely for a SYS-01 export: about 5,200 tickets held passcodes)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p))

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the shop (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the ticketing and POS vendor, its AI model provider, the backup provider, or the data recovery lab) has a breach of a system it maintains for the shop
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the agent must give the shop the information it needs to notify. The shop still sends the notices

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 4% of customers give an out-of-state address; counsel applies each state's law

trigger: Suspected theft of customer data or devices by a workforce member, or a criminal compromise of card data or accounts
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0-2); coordinate with counsel before contacting police about an employee
notify: Local police (insider theft); FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office (card data or account compromise)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. Applies to all U.S. persons

trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the shop extends no credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314 (P03 G-141)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the shop is below its SBA size standard
